Keywords: heatmap, density, matrix, intensity, calendar, correlation, grid, sequential scale
Looks Like: A grid of square or rectangular cells whose fill shows size of a value, with row and column labels and a legend bar. Cells touch or have thin gaps, and the surrounding page is plain.
Use When: analysts, operations teams, product managers, researchers, anyone comparing many categories over time or across two dimensions
Avoid When: Avoid for fewer than about 12 values, where a bar chart reads faster, or when exact numbers matter more than patterns.
Palette: Use one sequential scale from light to dark in a single hue family, or a diverging scale with a neutral midpoint for above and below a baseline. Start: #F7FBFF empty or low, #6BAED6 middle, #08306B high, #B2182B and #2166AC for diverging ends, #FFFFFF page.
Type Approach: Plain sans-serif such as IBM Plex Sans or Inter. Axis labels at 12 to 13 px, tabular numerals, cell values in 11 px only where the cell is large enough.
Layout: Matrix on a strict grid, cells at least 24 px square, labels sticky on scroll, legend beside or above with the numeric range. Dense, with the chart taking most of the width.
Motion: Cells fade to a new colour over 200 ms ease-out when data changes; tooltip appears in 120 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: rainbow scales that have no order; a red-to-green scale that colour-blind users cannot read; heat maps with no legend or no numbers on hover
Accessibility: Never rely on colour alone (1.4.1): add values on hover and focus, and a table view. Use a lightness-ordered scale that survives greyscale. Cell boundaries need 3:1 against neighbours where they carry meaning (1.4.11). Make cells keyboard-focusable with a visible ring (2.4.7).
Performance: medium: hundreds or thousands of cells; draw with canvas or SVG rects and avoid per-cell DOM listeners.
Checklist: Scale is ordered by lightness; Legend shows the numeric range; Every cell has a value on hover and focus; A table alternative exists; Checked in greyscale

Keywords: executive, kpi, summary, scorecard, board, overview, trend, headline numbers
Looks Like: One screen with four to six large headline numbers, each with a small trend line and a change against last period. Below sit two or three charts with plain titles that state the finding.
Use When: directors, founders, managers reviewing results weekly, board packs, investor updates
Avoid When: Avoid for people who must investigate causes or act on single records; they need drill-down and tables, not a summary.
Palette: Mostly neutral with one accent for the main series and two status colours used sparingly. Start: #FFFFFF page, #F4F5F7 panels, #1F2933 text, #0B5FA5 accent, #B42318 bad, #1B7F4B good.
Type Approach: One sans family with a strong numeric look, such as Inter or Source Sans 3, with tabular numerals. Headline figures 40 to 56 px semibold, labels 14 px, chart text 12 px.
Layout: 12-column grid, KPI row first, then charts; 24 px gaps. Low density: no more than about 8 elements above the fold, nothing that needs scrolling to get the point.
Motion: Numbers count up once over 600 ms ease-out on first load; nothing loops. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: twelve identical tiles with no priority; gauges and donut charts for everything; green and red arrows with no baseline or period named
Accessibility: Pair every red or green with an arrow or word (1.4.1). Keep 4.5:1 text contrast on panels (1.4.3). Give each chart a text summary and a data table link. Reflow to one column at 320 px (1.4.10).
Performance: low: a few small charts and text; one chart library or plain SVG is enough.
Checklist: Each KPI names its period and baseline; Status uses words or icons as well as colour; Titles state a finding; Works at 320 px width

Keywords: monitoring, live, streaming, alerts, uptime, latency, operations, status
Looks Like: A dense, dark screen of line charts, a few status tiles and an alert list ordered by severity. Values refresh in place and the time axis scrolls.
Use When: engineers, operations teams, support leads, logistics control rooms, anyone watching a system that changes by the second
Avoid When: Avoid for occasional-use reports and for audiences who need calm summaries; constant change is tiring and hard to read.
Palette: Dark neutral base so data stands out, with colour kept for state. Start: #0F1419 page, #1A222B panels, #D7DEE5 text, #4DA3FF primary series, #F5A524 warning, #FF5C5C critical.
Type Approach: Clean sans such as IBM Plex Sans paired with IBM Plex Mono for timestamps and IDs only. Tabular numerals everywhere, 12 to 14 px, never smaller.
Layout: Compact grid with 8 px gaps, status strip on top, alerts in a fixed column on the right. High density, but with one clearly largest panel.
Motion: Update values without animation; highlight a changed value with a 300 ms background flash. Provide a pause control. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: a pulsing green dot when nothing is live; red and green only for state; every chart auto-refreshing at one second with no pause
Accessibility: Provide a pause or freeze control (2.2.2) for anything that updates for over five seconds. Announce new critical alerts through a polite live region, not each data point. Add icons or words to status colour (1.4.1). Keep 4.5:1 text on dark panels (1.4.3).
Performance: high: continuous updates and many series; throttle redraws, window the data and use canvas for long time ranges.
Checklist: A pause control exists; Status is never colour alone; Alerts are ordered by severity; Timestamps show the time zone; Stale data is marked as stale

Keywords: drill-down, hierarchy, breadcrumb, filters, detail, explore, tables, segments
Looks Like: A summary chart at the top level; selecting a bar or segment replaces it with the next level and shows the path taken above. A table of the underlying rows sits underneath.
Use When: analysts, finance teams, support managers, anyone asking why a number moved
Avoid When: Avoid when users only need the headline; deep navigation hides the overview and costs them time.
Palette: Neutral page, one accent for the selected item, a muted grey for the rest. Start: #FFFFFF page, #E3E7EB unselected bars, #1D4ED8 selected, #111827 text, #6B7280 secondary text.
Type Approach: A legible sans such as Source Sans 3 or Inter. Table text 14 px with tabular numerals, right-aligned numbers, left-aligned labels.
Layout: Chart above, table below, filters in a single bar. The path (All regions > North > Leeds) shows the current level and each part is a link back. Medium to high density.
Motion: On drill, the new chart replaces the old in 250 ms with a short slide of bars; the path updates at once. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: modal on top of modal for each level; a drill path hidden in the URL only; charts that cannot be reached by keyboard
Accessibility: Every bar and segment must be a button reachable by Tab, with a visible ring (2.4.7). Keep the back path as links and update the page title. Target sizes at least 24 px (2.5.8). Selected state needs more than colour (1.4.1): add a heavier outline.
Performance: medium: data fetched per level; load lazily and cache earlier levels.
Checklist: Every level is reachable by keyboard; The path links back; The table matches the chart; URL holds the current level; Selected state is not colour alone

Aliases: Side-by-Side Comparison|Benchmark View|Before and After|Period Comparison
Keywords: comparison, benchmark, versus, side-by-side, variance, period, difference, small multiples
Looks Like: Two or more series placed on the same axis or in matched small charts, with a difference column and the baseline always in the same place. Titles name what is compared.
Use When: finance teams, marketers, product teams, researchers comparing periods, regions, plans or versions
Avoid When: Avoid when there is nothing sensible to compare against, or when more than about five series would make the chart unreadable.
Palette: Two clearly different colours for the two things compared, plus neutral grey for context. Start: #FFFFFF page, #005AB5 for A, #DC8A00 for B, #5C6770 neutral, #1B1B1B text.
Type Approach: Sans with tabular numerals such as Inter or IBM Plex Sans. Same size and weight for each side so neither seems more important.
Layout: Equal-width columns or small multiples sharing the same scale, a variance column in the middle or at the right. Medium density, a shared y-axis starting at zero for bars.
Motion: Switching the comparison animates bars over 250 ms ease-in-out; nothing else moves. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: dual axes with different scales that fake a correlation; truncated bar axes; red and green as the only difference between series
Accessibility: Blue and orange stay distinguishable for most colour-blind users, but also vary line style or direct-label the series (1.4.1). Put direct labels on lines instead of a legend. Give a data table for each chart and keep 3:1 against the page for lines and bars (1.4.11).
Performance: low: static charts and simple data; small multiples cost little.
Checklist: Both sides share one scale; The baseline is named; Series are told apart without colour; Direct labels replace the legend

Keywords: forecast, prediction, confidence interval, scenario, projection, trend, model, uncertainty
Looks Like: Line charts where history is a solid line and the forecast continues as a dashed line inside a shaded band showing the range. A divider marks today.
Use When: demand planners, finance teams, energy and logistics analysts, anyone planning from a model
Avoid When: Avoid when the model is weak or the data thin; a confident-looking forecast misleads more than no forecast.
Palette: Solid colour for history, a lighter tint of the same colour for the forecast band, and one marker colour for today. Start: #FFFFFF page, #1F4E79 history, #9DB9D6 forecast band, #C2410C today marker, #2B2B2B text.
Type Approach: Sans such as Inter with tabular numerals. Label the range in words ('likely between 410 and 470'), not only as a shaded area.
Layout: One large chart with a scenario selector at the side, assumptions listed beside it. Medium density; the range and the model date always visible.
Motion: Changing a scenario redraws the forecast over 400 ms ease-in-out; history stays still. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: a single confident line with no range; gradient fills to make the forecast look exciting; showing accuracy figures nobody has measured
Accessibility: The forecast must differ from history by dash pattern and label, not by tint only (1.4.1). Provide the numbers in a table and state the range in text. Scenario controls need labels and a visible ring (2.4.7). Band edges 3:1 (1.4.11).
Performance: medium: model output may be heavy; compute on the server and send the series, not the model.
Checklist: Forecast is marked by line style and label; The range is stated in words; Model date and assumptions are shown; A data table exists

Aliases: Product Analytics|Funnel and Cohort View|Session Analytics|Engagement Dashboard
Keywords: funnel, cohort, retention, sessions, events, conversion, engagement, segments
Looks Like: A funnel chart of steps with drop-off percentages, a cohort retention table shaded by value, and a line chart of active users. A segment filter sits at the top.
Use When: product managers, growth teams, UX researchers, small online shops checking where visitors leave
Avoid When: Avoid with too little traffic for percentages to mean anything, and where tracking needs consent you do not have.
Palette: Neutral page with one hue for volume and a second for the segment being compared. Start: #FAFAFA page, #0F766E main series, #7C3AED comparison segment, #374151 text, #D1D5DB grid lines.
Type Approach: Sans like Inter or DM Sans. Tabular numerals, percentages with one decimal at most, step names in full words.
Layout: Funnel at left, cohort table at right, trend line across the bottom. Medium to high density; every chart shows its sample size.
Motion: Filter changes update charts in 200 ms with a cross-fade; no looping animation. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: vanity totals with no rate; funnels that hide the drop-off; session replays or heatmaps shown without a privacy note
Accessibility: Funnel steps need text labels and values, not colour only (1.4.1). Cohort cells carry numbers. Keep 4.5:1 text on shaded cells (1.4.3). Filters are native selects or buttons with labels.
Performance: medium: aggregate events on the server; never ship raw event logs to the browser.
Checklist: Sample sizes shown; Rates always sit beside counts; Consent and privacy stated; Funnel steps are labelled in words

Aliases: Finance Overview|Accounts Dashboard|Cash Flow View|Portfolio Dashboard
Keywords: finance, cash flow, revenue, budget, accounts, portfolio, variance, currency
Looks Like: Balances and cash position as large figures, a waterfall or bar chart of income against spend, and a ledger table with right-aligned, tabular numbers in the right currency.
Use When: accountants, finance managers, small business owners, treasurers, investors tracking holdings
Avoid When: Avoid for casual users who only want one figure; it can look heavier than the job needs.
Palette: Restrained palette: ink, one brand colour, and two status colours that are never the sole signal. Start: #FFFFFF page, #0F2A43 headings and primary, #0E7C66 income, #B3261E spend, #EEF1F4 table stripes.
Type Approach: A serious sans such as IBM Plex Sans or Source Sans 3. Tabular, lining numerals; negative values with a minus sign or brackets, not colour only.
Layout: Summary figures on top, chart in the middle, ledger table below. Dense but regular: 8 px base, 40 px rows, totals row fixed at the bottom.
Motion: Minimal: row hover colour in 100 ms; chart bars grow once in 300 ms ease-out. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: red and green numbers with no sign; candlestick charts for people who do not trade; unexplained rounding of money
Accessibility: Negative values need a sign or brackets as well as colour (1.4.1). Right-align numbers and keep the decimal point in line. Table needs header cells and captions. 4.5:1 for all figures (1.4.3). Sort buttons need a visible ring (2.4.7).
Performance: low: mostly tables and a few charts; paginate long ledgers.
Checklist: Currency and period are shown; Negatives have a sign; Numbers are right-aligned and tabular; Totals reconcile with the chart

Aliases: Sales Pipeline Dashboard|CRM Dashboard|Revenue Pipeline|Sales Ops View
Keywords: sales, pipeline, quota, deals, forecast, leads, win rate, territory
Looks Like: A pipeline by stage as horizontal bars, quota attainment per rep as bullet charts, and a list of deals closing this month with owner and value.
Use When: sales managers, account executives, revenue operations, small teams tracking leads and deals
Avoid When: Avoid for teams without clean CRM data; the dashboard will show gaps and not insight.
Palette: Neutral base, one strong colour for pipeline and a contrasting one for target markers. Start: #FFFFFF page, #14213D pipeline, #E07A00 target marker, #2A9D8F won, #F1F3F5 panels.
Type Approach: Sans such as Inter or Work Sans. Currency in tabular numerals with units in the header, deal names left-aligned at 14 px.
Layout: Stage bars left, rep list right, deals table under both. Medium-high density; a date range and owner filter in one bar at the top.
Motion: Bars grow once in 300 ms ease-out on load; deal rows highlight in 100 ms on hover. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: leaderboards that shame the bottom rep; funnel with invented conversion numbers; pie chart of lead sources
Accessibility: Bullet charts need text values for target and actual (1.4.1). Table has headers and sortable columns with visible focus (2.4.7). Targets 24 px or larger (2.5.8). Colours 3:1 against the panel (1.4.11).
Performance: low: aggregate numbers and small tables; fetch deals on demand.
Checklist: Targets and actuals are written as numbers; Stages are in funnel order; Filters have labels; Currency and period shown

Keywords: neubrutalism, hard shadow, thick border, flat colour, bold, playful, offset shadow, chunky
Looks Like: Flat saturated blocks of colour, thick black outlines and hard offset shadows with no blur. Buttons look like physical slabs and move when pressed.
Use When: startups with personality, creator tools, indie shops, events, youth brands, portfolios that want to be remembered
Avoid When: Avoid for banks, clinics and legal sites where the tone must be calm; and for long reading, where heavy boxes tire the eye.
Palette: Two or three loud flat colours on a pale ground, always with black ink. Start: #FFF8E7 page, #000000 ink and borders, #FF6B6B coral, #4D96FF blue, #FFD93D yellow.
Type Approach: Heavy grotesque such as Space Grotesk or Archivo Black for headings, a plain sans for body at 17 to 18 px. Sizes jump sharply between levels.
Layout: Blocky grid, 3 px borders, 6 px offset shadows, generous gutters. Not every block needs a box: bordered boxes on everything is the trap.
Motion: Press moves the element 4 px toward its shadow in 80 ms linear; hover shifts it 2 px. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: a bordered box around every block; one pastel per section with no logic; thick borders on text inputs and body cards alike
Accessibility: Borders help contrast (1.4.11) but check text on coloured blocks at 4.5:1 (1.4.3); yellow with white text fails. Keep a focus ring distinct from the border, such as 3 px offset outline (2.4.7). Targets 44 px.
Performance: low: borders and flat fills only; no images needed.
Checklist: Boxes only where they group something; Text on colour passes 4.5:1; Focus ring is distinct from borders; Press state works by keyboard; Body text stays plain and readable

Aliases: Bento Layout|Modular Tile Grid|Feature Grid|Apple-Style Tiles
Keywords: bento, grid, tiles, modular, feature grid, asymmetric, dashboard, product page
Looks Like: A page of rectangular tiles in different spans, each holding one idea: a large photo, a number, a short claim. Gaps are even and corners share one radius.
Use When: product pages, portfolios, feature overviews, personal sites, app landing pages with four to seven distinct points
Avoid When: Avoid when every tile says the same thing, or for linear content such as articles and legal text.
Palette: A neutral ground with two or three tile colours, chosen so the larger tiles carry the identity. Start: #F2F2F0 ground, #FFFFFF tile, #18181B text, #2F5D50 brand tile, #E9C46A highlight tile.
Type Approach: One sturdy sans such as Manrope or DM Sans, with a clear size step between tile titles and body. Keep text short; tiles are not paragraphs.
Layout: CSS grid with 4 or 6 columns, tiles spanning 1 to 2 cells, a 16 px gap and one corner radius. Collapse to a single column under 640 px, with the most important tile first.
Motion: Tiles may lift 4 px on hover in 200 ms ease-out; no staggered scroll reveals. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: a grid of identical rounded cards; icon tile above every heading; mock app screens with unreadable detail
Accessibility: Reading order must match visual order; use DOM order, not grid placement tricks (2.4.3 focus order). Each tile that is a link needs one link, not nested ones. Reflow at 320 px (1.4.10).
Performance: low: static layout; lazy-load the images and give them width and height.
Checklist: Tiles differ in size for a reason; DOM order matches reading order; One column under 640 px; Each tile holds one idea

Aliases: Y2K|Millennium Style|Frutiger Aero Lite|Late-90s Web Revival
Keywords: y2k, chrome, bubbles, metallic, glossy, 2000s, retro future, tech optimism
Looks Like: Glossy buttons, chrome and silver gradients, translucent plastic panels and rounded bubble shapes against sky blue and white. Feels like an early-2000s music player or desktop theme.
Use When: fashion, music, nostalgia brands, events, game and toy sites, youth culture, merch shops
Avoid When: Avoid for serious services such as law, medicine and finance, and for sites where text-heavy reading matters.
Palette: Cool metallics and candy colours with white highlights. Start: #E6F2FF sky ground, #9EC5F8 aqua panel, #C9CED6 silver, #FF4FA3 hot pink accent, #1B2A41 text.
Type Approach: Rounded geometric type such as Quicksand or Fredoka for headings, a plain sans for body. Keep body copy off glossy surfaces.
Layout: Centred, boxy page with bevelled panels, 12 px radii, inset highlights. Medium density; decorate the frame, not the text area.
Motion: Buttons brighten in 150 ms ease-out; one slow shine passes across a hero object over 1200 ms once. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: gradients on every surface; blurry glow behind the hero; sparkle icons as decoration
Accessibility: Gloss lowers text contrast: put text on solid areas at 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Do not rely on shine to show a button state (1.4.11). Avoid flashing or looping shine (2.2.2, 2.3.3).
Performance: medium: layered gradients and shadows cost paint time; use few layers and flat colour for large areas.
Checklist: Text sits on solid areas; Gloss is limited to controls and frames; Focus ring is visible; Nothing loops; The look is chosen by the brand, not by default

Aliases: Neon Dystopia|Sci-Fi Terminal|Night City Style|Hacker Interface
Keywords: cyberpunk, neon, terminal, sci-fi, dark, glitch, hud, game
Looks Like: Near-black ground with hard neon lines in cyan and magenta, angled cut corners, thin HUD frames and scan-line detail. Type is wide and technical.
Use When: games, esports, music events, sci-fi fiction, hardware and security brands, hackathons
Avoid When: Avoid for health, education and finance, and for anything read for long; neon on black tires the eye.
Palette: Dark base with two neon accents and one warning colour. Start: #0B0B14 ground, #00F0FF cyan lines, #FF2A6D magenta accent, #F5E642 warning, #D8DEE9 body text.
Type Approach: Wide display face such as Orbitron or Chakra Petch for headings only; a plain sans such as Rajdhani or Inter for body. Monospace only for code or data.
Layout: Angled corners via clip-path, 1 px neon rules, panels on a 12-column grid. Keep body copy in solid dark panels with large margins.
Motion: A 120 ms glitch offset on hover only; a 600 ms line draw on first load. No continuous flicker. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: near-black with one acid accent used on everything; glow behind every heading; ASCII or dithered images as a style
Accessibility: Neon on black passes contrast but flicker and glitch can trigger problems (2.3.1, 2.3.3). Never animate body text. Keep 4.5:1 for body (1.4.3) and a visible focus ring in a third colour (2.4.7).
Performance: medium: glow and filter effects are costly; prefer borders and flat fills to blur filters.
CSS Starter:
.hud { background: #11121F; border: var(--line); color: var(--ink); clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - var(--cut)) 0, 100% var(--cut), 100% 100%, var(--cut) 100%, 0 calc(100% - var(--cut))); }
.hud :is(a, button):focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--warn); outline-offset: 3px; }
Checklist: No flashing above three times a second; Body text on solid panels; Glitch only on hover; Focus ring in a separate colour

Keywords: organic, biophilic, nature, earthy, curves, botanical, soft, wellbeing
Looks Like: Curved, irregular shapes, leaf and stone forms, natural photography and textures such as paper or linen. Colours come from soil, leaf and water.
Use When: wellness, gardens, landscaping, ethical food, outdoor brands, eco products, retreats, farm shops
Avoid When: Avoid for data-heavy tools and for brands with no genuine link to nature; green on its own does not make a brand natural.
Palette: Muted earth colours with one deeper green for actions. Start: #F3EFE6 ground, #3F6B4F leaf green, #8C6A4F soil brown, #D7A95B ochre, #26332B text.
Type Approach: A humanist serif such as Fraunces or Lora for headings with a friendly sans such as Nunito Sans for body. Generous line height of 1.6.
Layout: Asymmetric flowing sections, large rounded image masks, wide margins and low density. Use photographs of plants, places and people, not stock.
Motion: Slow 600 ms ease-out lift on images on first view; small sway of one decorative leaf at most. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: cream background with terracotta accent by default; leaf icons on every heading; squircle masks on every image
Accessibility: Green on brown can fail contrast: check 4.5:1 (1.4.3) and 3:1 for controls (1.4.11). Decorative curves must not clip text at 320 px (1.4.10). Provide alt text for photographs.
Performance: medium: large photographs and masks; serve responsive images in AVIF or WebP.
Checklist: Photos are of the actual place; Green and brown meet contrast; Shapes never clip text; Body is 17 px or more

Keywords: ai, chat, assistant, prompt, streaming, generative, copilot, agent
Looks Like: A prompt box as the main control, messages that stream in, sources and actions beside each answer, and plain controls to retry, edit or stop. The layout leaves space around the text.
Use When: AI products, assistants inside tools, search and writing helpers, support bots, agent dashboards
Avoid When: Avoid when a normal form or button does the job faster; a chat box for a task with three fields is a step back.
Palette: Neutral surface with one accent for the assistant and a clear user tint. Start: #FFFFFF page, #F5F5F7 assistant bubbles, #E8F0FE user messages, #1A1A1A text, #1A56DB accent.
Type Approach: One readable sans such as Inter or Public Sans at 16 to 17 px, line length 65 characters; Source Code Pro only for code blocks.
Layout: Single central column of 720 px, prompt pinned at the bottom, sources and tools in a collapsible side panel. Low density; the answer is the focus.
Motion: Text streams as it arrives; a 150 ms fade for new blocks; a visible Stop button. No typing-dot loops beyond a few seconds. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: purple-to-blue gradient and aurora backgrounds; sparkle icons marking everything as AI; a fake typing delay on instant answers
Accessibility: Announce streamed answers through a polite live region once complete, not per token. Provide a Stop control (2.2.2). Label the prompt field, keep 4.5:1 (1.4.3), and make retry, copy and edit proper buttons at 24 px or more (2.5.8). Mark AI-written content plainly.
Performance: medium: streaming and long lists; virtualise long conversations and render code blocks lazily.
Checklist: A Stop control exists; Sources are shown beside answers; Streaming is announced once; AI content is labelled; Prompt field is labelled

Keywords: memphis, 80s, postmodern, squiggle, confetti, geometric, pattern, playful
Looks Like: Clashing flat colours, black squiggles, triangles, circles and dotted patterns scattered at angles. Shapes overlap text areas but never sit behind them.
Use When: children's brands, creative studios, festivals, design schools, cafes, toy and stationery shops
Avoid When: Avoid for serious or data-heavy sites; the pattern noise competes with content and looks flippant for law, clinics or banks.
Palette: Primary and pastel colours used flat, with black for line work. Start: #FFFFFF ground, #FF3EA5 pink, #00C2A8 teal, #FFD23F yellow, #1B1B1B line work and text.
Type Approach: Chunky geometric display such as Poppins or Lexend Giga at heading sizes with a plain sans body. Keep body on a flat, blank panel.
Layout: Offset grid with deliberate tilt on shapes, big margins, text on solid blocks. Medium density; limit shapes to the margins and one hero area.
Motion: Shapes drift 8 px in 4000 ms ease-in-out once; hover rotates a shape 6 degrees in 200 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: confetti patterns behind body text; every shape in every colour; ironic squiggles used with no link to the brand
Accessibility: Patterns behind text break contrast (1.4.3): keep text on solid fills. Decorative shapes get aria-hidden and empty alt. Looping drift must be stoppable or absent (2.2.2).
Performance: low: mostly SVG shapes and flat colour.
Checklist: Body text sits on solid fill; Shapes are aria-hidden; Pattern is confined to margins; No loops that cannot be stopped

Keywords: vaporwave, synthwave, retro, 80s, pastel, pink, grid, statue
Looks Like: A pink and cyan sunset palette, a perspective grid floor, classical busts, Japanese katakana and early-computer windows. Slightly ironic and nostalgic.
Use When: music, art projects, nightlife, indie games, merch, creative portfolios
Avoid When: Avoid for businesses where trust and clarity come first; the irony does not read as serious service.
Palette: Pastel pinks and aquas against deep violet or navy. Start: #1B1033 night, #FF71CE pink, #01CDFE cyan, #B967FF violet, #FFFB96 pale yellow for sparse highlights.
Type Approach: Wide display face such as Syne or Monoton for headings only; a simple sans such as Space Grotesk for body. Katakana as ornament only if it is accurate.
Layout: Centred hero with a horizon line, grid floor in CSS, content in solid windows. Low to medium density; one image focus per screen.
Motion: Grid floor scrolls in a 4000 ms linear loop only in the hero, with a visible pause. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: gradient backgrounds on every section; purple-to-blue washes; random Japanese text with no meaning
Accessibility: Looping grid motion needs a pause control (2.2.2) and a static fallback. Pink on violet text must reach 4.5:1 (1.4.3): test every pairing. Never place text on the animated floor.
Performance: medium: large gradient areas and an animated plane; use transform on a single layer.
CSS Starter:
.floor { background: linear-gradient(var(--night), #2A1650); background-image: linear-gradient(var(--cyan) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, var(--cyan) 1px, transparent 1px); background-size: var(--grid) var(--grid); transform: perspective(300px) rotateX(55deg); }
.window { background: #241545; border: 2px solid var(--pink); color: #FFFFFF; }
Checklist: Text sits on solid windows; Moving floor can be paused; Colour pairs meet 4.5:1; Katakana is accurate

Keywords: depth, layers, parallax, z-axis, shadow, stacked, elevation, overlap
Looks Like: Surfaces stacked at different heights with consistent shadows and overlap. Foreground items sit over background planes and shift slightly as the page moves.
Use When: product launches, portfolios, storytelling pages, hotels, architecture, exhibition sites
Avoid When: Avoid for content-heavy pages and for low-power phones; depth that moves slows the page and can cause motion sickness.
Palette: Light tints for far planes and stronger contrast for near ones, so depth is shown by colour as well as shadow. Start: #ECEFF3 back plane, #FFFFFF mid plane, #11161C front text, #3558A5 accent, #C9D1DB edge.
Type Approach: Sturdy sans such as Manrope or Outfit with two clear weights; foreground type is larger and heavier than background type.
Layout: Three planes at most: background, content, overlay. Overlap by 24 to 48 px; keep the reading column clear of any overlap.
Motion: Parallax of 20 px or less, transform only, 300 ms ease-out for entrances. One heavy effect per screen. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: every section fades and slides in on scroll; shadows of different strength and angle on each card; parallax over text
Accessibility: Parallax can cause vestibular symptoms: remove it under reduced motion (2.3.3). Overlaps must not hide text or focus rings (2.4.11). Use shadows consistently so depth is meaningful.
Performance: high: stacked layers and scroll-linked transforms; promote only the moving layers and test on a mid-range phone.
Checklist: Three planes at most; One shadow system; Overlap never covers text or focus; Parallax is off under reduced motion

Aliases: Maximal Minimalism|Oversized Type Minimal|Bold Whitespace|Extreme Minimal
Keywords: minimalism, oversized, whitespace, bold type, sparse, statement, editorial, monochrome
Looks Like: Very little on screen: one huge word or image, large empty areas and tiny supporting text. Everything else is cut, so the one thing left is hard to miss.
Use When: architects, photographers, fashion labels, galleries, studios, single-product launches
Avoid When: Avoid for stores, services or tools with many options; users must find information fast and sparse pages hide it.
Palette: Black and white with one accent used once. Start: #FFFFFF ground, #0A0A0A ink, #E4E4E4 hairlines, #D62E1F single accent.
Type Approach: One strong face, either a grotesque such as Archivo or a serif with a reason from the brand. Headline at 12 to 20 vw with fluid clamp(); support text at 16 px, not smaller.
Layout: Single column or a two-point layout with 120 px or more of space. Low density, one idea per screen, navigation as plain text links.
Motion: One 500 ms ease-out reveal of the headline per page; links underline in 120 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: tiny grey body text that fails contrast; cream ground with terracotta accent; tight negative letter-spacing on every heading
Accessibility: Large type must still reflow at 320 px without clipping (1.4.10). Light grey supporting text often fails 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Do not hide navigation behind an unlabelled icon. Keep visible focus (2.4.7).
Performance: low: little content, few assets, plain CSS.
CSS Starter:
.statement { font-size: var(--display); line-height: 0.9; font-weight: 700; margin-block: var(--space); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.small { font-size: var(--body-size); color: var(--ink); max-width: 38ch; }
Checklist: One idea per screen; Support text is 16 px and passes contrast; Large type does not clip at 320 px; Navigation is labelled in words

Keywords: kinetic, typography, animated text, variable font, marquee, scroll type, motion, headline
Looks Like: Letters and words that move, stretch or change weight as the user scrolls or hovers. The type is the main image on the page.
Use When: portfolios, agencies, music and film, event posters, campaign sites, studios showing craft
Avoid When: Avoid for trust sites, long reading, and visitors with vestibular or reading difficulties; moving text is harder to read.
Palette: Restrained colours so the movement is the point: one ground, one ink, one accent. Start: #F2F0EB ground, #101010 ink, #FF5A1F accent, #2B2B2B secondary.
Type Approach: A variable font such as Anybody or Bricolage Grotesque, animating weight or width. Keep body copy static in a plain face at 17 px.
Layout: Large type zones with plain text areas between them. Low density; each moving word has a static twin in the markup.
Motion: Weight shifts over 400 ms ease-in-out on hover; scroll-linked stretch uses transform and font-variation-settings under 600 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: scrolling marquee on every page; every heading animating on scroll; text that moves while the reader tries to read it
Accessibility: Animated text needs a pause or stop (2.2.2) and removal under reduced motion (2.3.3). Do not move body copy. Text must stay selectable and readable by screen readers: keep one proper heading, not letter-by-letter spans without a label.
Performance: high: font variation and scroll-linked updates are costly; limit moving text to one block per screen.
Checklist: One moving text block per screen; Heading is an h1 element with a text label; Body text is static; A pause exists for loops; Tested under reduced motion

Keywords: craft, workshop, maker, joiner, potter, brewery, artisan, process, materials, small producer
Looks Like: Photographs of hands, tools, raw materials and finished pieces, with process shown in order and the people named. Paper, timber and clay tones sit behind plain, readable text.
Use When: joiners, potters, breweries, bakers, furniture makers, jewellers, small producers, farm shops, tailors
Avoid When: Avoid for large chains, or where nobody can show the actual workshop; a craft look without a genuine process is worse than a plain one.
Palette: Muted material colours taken from the work itself, with one strong accent from a product or glaze. Start: #F4EFE6 paper, #3B2F26 dark timber for text, #A5522D fired clay accent, #5E6B4E moss, #D9CDB8 stone.
Type Approach: A sturdy serif such as Source Serif 4 or Newsreader for headings and a clear sans such as Work Sans for body at 17 px. Prices and sizes in tabular numerals.
Layout: Photo-led sections: materials, steps, finished work, people, how to order. Medium density, one column for reading, product grid with a visible price and lead time.
Motion: A soft 250 ms image fade on page load and a 150 ms hover on products. No pinned scenes. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: stock photos of hands and wood; a brown and cream colour scheme used as a default; process steps as a three-box how-it-works strip
Accessibility: Photographs need descriptive alt text (1.1.1 for images). Text over photos needs a solid scrim at 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Order forms need labels and error text. Targets 44 px on phones.
Performance: medium: photograph-heavy; serve AVIF or WebP with width and height, lazy-load below the fold.
Checklist: Photos are of the owner's workshop; Each material and step is named; People are named with owner approval; Price and lead time are visible; Contact and order route are one tap away

Keywords: clinic, dentist, physio, pharmacy, booking, trust, calm, healthcare, appointment, patient
Looks Like: A white page with plain blue-green accents, large readable text, a prominent Book button, opening hours and the practitioners with a photo and qualification. Nothing moves except focus and hover.
Use When: clinics, dentists, physiotherapists, pharmacies, opticians, vets, therapists, GP surgeries
Avoid When: Avoid for brands that need personality or youth appeal; it is deliberately plain and will not stand out by looks alone.
Palette: Clean whites and one cool accent, with a separate colour for warnings only. Start: #FFFFFF page, #0F5C6E trust teal, #E8F3F5 soft panel, #1B2A33 text, #B42318 urgent notice.
Type Approach: A clear humanist sans such as Atkinson Hyperlegible or Source Sans 3. Body 18 px, line height 1.6, no thin weights, no all-caps.
Layout: Single column on phones: Book, call, address, hours at the top. Low density, plain section headings, fees and services in simple lists, 64 px between sections.
Motion: Hover and focus changes in 120 ms; one gentle reveal at most. No video backgrounds or pinned scenes. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, drop all of it and show the end state.
Slop Habits: stock photos of smiling models with a stethoscope; a blue gradient hero; claims such as best in town that nobody can check
Accessibility: Booking form: labelled fields, clear errors, no time limits that cut off users (2.2.1). Phone number as a tap link. 4.5:1 text (1.4.3), visible focus ring and not obscured (2.4.7, 2.4.11), targets 44 px (2.5.8). Say what happens in an emergency.
Performance: low: mainly text and a few staff photos; no heavy scripts besides booking.
Checklist: Book and phone are above the fold; Hours, address and fees are visible; Staff qualifications are stated and checked; Forms are labelled with clear errors; Emergency advice is stated
